meta.title: Zheng Zhang · Personal Website
meta.description: Zheng Zhang — graduate researcher and product strategy practitioner exploring data, AI, and economic decision-making.
meta.ogDescription: Research, product thinking, data analysis, and the stories in between.

home.heroDescription: A master's student at Beijing Institute of Technology, with a background in finance and energy & climate economics. My work sits at the intersection of quantitative research, AI-enabled product strategy, and real-world problem solving.

about.aboutIntro: I enjoy making sense of complexity — whether that means uncovering a pattern in research data, designing a product strategy around user behavior, or turning repetitive work into a useful tool.
about.aboutBodyBefore: My training began in finance and expanded into energy and climate economics. Along the way, I explored applied analytics and product strategy through internships at Kuaishou, JD.com, and DiDi. Across different settings, I keep returning to the same question:
about.aboutBodyEmphasis: what is the real problem, and how can we measure that we've solved it?

education.edu1Detail: Interdisciplinary studies in economic analysis, energy systems, and policy modeling
education.edu2Detail: Finance, quantitative analysis, and business decision-making

experience.experienceSummary: Experiences across consumer internet products, automation, and cross-functional operations.
experience.exp1Body: Worked on push notification experience and growth strategy, combining user segmentation, predictive modeling, interpretable analytics, and LLM-assisted insight generation to inform more precise outreach.
experience.exp2Body: Built Python-based workflows to automate high-frequency rebate checks. Applied text processing, TF-IDF, and clustering to analyze customer feedback and surface recurring service issues.
experience.exp3Body: Helped standardize multi-city project workflows, coordinate operational milestones, and work across business, customer service, and legal teams to support delivery.

research.researchSummary: My academic work uses quantitative methods to examine the interaction between finance, energy transition, and sustainability.
research.paperDesc: Student first-author research examining nonlinear effects and spatial spillovers in the relationship between green finance and clean energy transition, using spatial econometrics and panel threshold methods.
research.research2Title: Household Clean Energy Transition: Decisions, Impacts & Policy
research.research2Body: Participated in research on the resource potential, economic value, and environmental benefits of end-of-life household appliance recovery, drawing on scenario analysis, material flow analysis, and life-cycle assessment.
research.researchFootnote: Full publication details and links can be added after verification.
research.research1Title: More Developed Less Efficient? Spatial Threshold Effects of Green Finance on Clean Energy Transition Based on SPDM-PTRM Model

projects.projectsAside: A few problems I've enjoyed tackling
projects.project1Title: Understanding Why Users Turn Off Notifications
projects.project1Body: Connected behavioral signals, user matching, and LLM-based explanation to explore notification fatigue and design more thoughtful engagement strategies.
projects.project2Body: Contributed to a multi-stage content discovery workflow that combines rule-based screening, ranking, and large-model quality assessment.
projects.project3Title: Turning Manual Checks into Python Workflows
projects.project3Body: Translated complex rebate rules into an automated verification process with rule matching, exception detection, and structured outputs.
projects.project4Title: Measuring the Effects of Green Finance
projects.project4Body: Studied threshold relationships and spatial effects in the clean energy transition through quantitative modeling and empirical analysis.
projects.projectsNote: Project descriptions are intentionally high-level for public viewing.
